descriptors.concept_name: Presentation and Disclosure of Revenue Contracts
descriptors.definition: An entity presents contracts in the balance sheet as a contract liability, contract asset, or receivable based on the relationship between performance and payment. Any unconditional right to consideration must be presented separately as a receivable.
inclusion: Presentation of contract liabilities when payment is received before performance
Presentation of contract assets or receivables when performance precedes payment
Separate presentation of excise duty in the statement of profit and loss
exclusion: Revenue from interest and dividends covered under financial instruments standards
nearby_distinctions: A contract asset conditions the right to consideration on something other than the passage of time, whereas a receivable represents an unconditional right requiring only the passage of time.

descriptors.definition: An entity presents contract balances in its balance sheet as a contract asset, contract liability, or receivable depending on whether goods or services have been transferred relative to customer payments. Unconditional rights to consideration are accounted for as receivables under Ind AS 109.
inclusion: Balance sheet classification of contract assets and liabilities
Separate presentation of excise duty in the statement of profit and loss
exclusion: Subsequent measurement rules governed by unrelated accounting standards
nearby_distinctions: Contract liabilities arise from advance payments or due dates prior to performance, whereas contract assets and receivables arise after performance occurs.

descriptors.definition: Entities must provide comprehensive disclosures regarding contracts with customers, including disaggregated revenue, contract balances, performance obligations, and transaction prices. These disclosures enable users to understand the nature, amount, timing, and uncertainty of revenue and cash flows.
inclusion: Disclosures of opening and closing contract balances
Information about performance obligations and transaction prices
Judgements made in determining timing and measurement
exclusion: General financial statement notes unrelated to customer contracts
nearby_distinctions: General disclosures provide high-level totals of revenue and impairments, whereas specific disclosures break down performance obligations, transaction prices, and significant judgements.

descriptors.definition: A service concession arrangement involves a private sector operator constructing or upgrading public infrastructure and operating and maintaining it for a specified period under a contract with a public sector grantor. The operator is contractually obligated to provide public services on behalf of the grantor.
inclusion: Arrangements described as build-operate-transfer or rehabilitate-operate-transfer
Contracts involving public-to-private infrastructure operations
exclusion: Infrastructure traditionally constructed and maintained solely by the public sector without private operator involvement
nearby_distinctions: Service concession arrangements obligate a private operator to deliver public services and manage infrastructure on behalf of a public grantor, unlike ordinary commercial supply contracts.

descriptors.definition: Service concession arrangements require an operator to construct, upgrade, operate, and maintain public infrastructure for a set duration while being paid for services through contractual mechanisms. The public sector grantor sets performance standards, pricing adjustment rules, and dispute resolution processes.
inclusion: Private sector management of public infrastructure such as roads, hospitals, and utilities
Contracts containing specified pricing and arbitration terms
exclusion: Arrangements where the private entity acts merely as an agent without management responsibilities
nearby_distinctions: The operator takes responsibility for management and operations rather than simply acting as an ordinary commercial agent.

descriptors.concept_name: Accounting Principles for Service Concession Arrangements
descriptors.definition: Infrastructure is not recognized as the operator's property, plant, and equipment because the arrangement does not convey the right to control its use. The operator accounts for construction and operation services under Ind AS 115, recognizing consideration as a financial asset or intangible asset.
inclusion: Recognition of financial assets when there is an unconditional right to receive cash from or at the direction of the grantor
Allocation of consideration based on relative fair values of delivered services
exclusion: Capitalization of public infrastructure as the operator's own property, plant and equipment
nearby_distinctions: The operator holds access rights to run the service rather than control-based ownership of the underlying public infrastructure.

descriptors.definition: Operators and grantors must disclose details of service concession arrangements, including arrangement descriptions, significant terms, asset use rights, obligations, and changes occurring during the period. Entities must also disclose revenue and profits or losses recognized from exchanging construction services for financial or intangible assets.
inclusion: Descriptions of significant terms affecting future cash flows
Nature and extent of renewal, termination, and overhaul obligations
Individual or class-based aggregation of arrangement disclosures
exclusion: Standard disclosures unrelated to public-private service concessions
nearby_distinctions: These disclosures specifically address public service concessions, distinct from standard revenue contract disclosures.

descriptors.concept_name: Extracts of Financial Statements of Listed Entity
descriptors.definition: Practical illustration material presenting real-world financial statement extracts and accounting policies regarding revenue from contracts with customers from a listed corporate entity.
inclusion: Annual report disclosures and policy excerpts from listed entities
nearby_distinctions: Provides empirical reporting examples rather than standard-setting text.

descriptors.concept_name: Significant Differences in Ind AS 115 vis-à-vis AS 7 and AS 9
descriptors.definition: Ind AS 115 introduces an overarching core principle based on a five-step model centered on transferring control of goods or services at a transaction price. In contrast, older standards like AS 7 and AS 9 lacked comprehensive multiple-element guidance and a unified control-based revenue framework.
inclusion: Comparison of framework definitions and multiple-element handling
Contrasts in revenue measurement and recognition triggers
exclusion: Detailed transition provisions between old and new standards
nearby_distinctions: Ind AS 115 mandates a control-based five-step model, whereas AS 7 and AS 9 measure revenue based on gross inflows or stage of completion without an overarching single standard framework.
